dascp.note: Formalizes the behavioural k-of-n approval core of C16-S; the 'periodic updates to address emerging security challenges' clause is operational and stays out of BPO scope.

iso20022.note: When a settlement transaction instruction requires multi-party validation, the property's k-of-n approval gate constrains whether the instruction can be admitted at the contract layer.

descriptions.semantic: Every privileged transaction in scope of the multiparty-validation policy takes effect only if it carries valid approvals from at least k of n authorized validators (with k and n defined by the policy in force when the transaction is processed). Each approval is a distinct, authenticated act by a distinct identity. The validator set V and the threshold k are themselves elements of the access-control state and change only via authorized governance operations.
descriptions.system_theoretic: A threshold-guard constraint on the labelled transition system: a transition labelled with a privileged operation o is enabled only when the accompanying approval multiset contains ≥ k entries each verifying under a distinct identity in the current validator set V; n = |V| at execution time. The threshold predicate is the dynamic residue of a static k-of-n access-control matrix; the configuration (V, k) is itself an invariant whose only legal mutations are authorized governance transitions.
descriptions.security: The collusion bound. A k-of-n policy converts unilateral compromise of a single validator into a non-event: an attacker must compromise k distinct validators to forge an approval set. Failure modes — counting the same signer twice, accepting expired/rotated keys, replaying an approval set across contexts, or letting the threshold itself be reset by an unprivileged action — defeat this bound; the property is the negation of those failure modes.
descriptions.execution_semantics: Realized by collecting EIP-712-typed signed approvals (each binding chain-id, contract, nonce, and operation digest), counting unique authorized signers, comparing against the threshold, and gating the privileged effect on the comparison. Violations live in: missing duplicate detection (two encodings of one signer counted twice), stale-set drift (signer was authorized at signing time but rotated out by execution time, or vice versa), missing domain separation (cross-chain or cross-contract replay), and write paths to V or k that are not themselves governance-gated.
descriptions.formal_verification: A 1-safety property: parametric rule over every privileged method asserting that, on the success path, |{ distinct authorized signers in the approval set }| ≥ k holds against the current (V, k); and that mutations of (V, k) are only by authorized governance operations. The signature-soundness side is delegated to BPO:0074; the access-control of the governance layer is delegated to BPO:0040; this property is the threshold logic that sits above both.

formalization.signature: Validators V(s) ⊆ Addr; threshold k(s) ∈ ℕ with k(s) ≤ |V(s)| = n(s); approval set A ⊆ Sig; sig: Addr × Msg → Sig (verified signature); privileged ⊆ Op; canonical signer identity id: Sig → Addr.
formalization.first_order_logic:
Threshold guard:  ∀ s, s', o, A . ( s --[o, A]--> s' ∧ o ∈ privileged ) → |{ id(σ) : σ ∈ A ∧ id(σ) ∈ V(s) ∧ sig.verify(id(σ), msg(o,s), σ) }| ≥ k(s).
Distinct counting:  the set above is over CANONICAL signer identity, so multiplicity of any one signer in A contributes at most 1.
Configuration integrity:  ∀ s, s', t . ( V(s') ≠ V(s) ∨ k(s') ≠ k(s) ) ∧ s --[t]--> s' → authorizedGovernance(t).

temporal_logic.ltl: G( privilegedEffect(o) → |distinct_authorized_signers(A)| ≥ k )   ∧   G( change(V) ∨ change(k) → authorizedGovernance )

formalization.state_machine: Two-layer automaton: (1) the protected-operation layer, each privileged edge gated by the threshold check against the current (V, k); (2) the governance layer, with edges that mutate V or k themselves gated by their own access-control. The property is that the protected layer's guards never accept an under-threshold approval set AND the governance layer mediates every change to (V, k).
formalization.type_theoretic: Approval as an affine (consumable, non-duplicable) witness keyed by (validator identity, operation digest); a privileged call is well-typed only when supplied a multiset of distinct approval witnesses of cardinality ≥ k from the current validator set. Distinct-signer counting becomes a static typing constraint rather than a fragile runtime nominal check.
formalization.algebraic: Approval multisets under (∪, ∅) form a commutative monoid; the threshold predicate is monotone in approval-set inclusion. (V, k) together form the access-control configuration, modified only by sanctioned governance transitions.

bindings.note: Direct (identity aspect): `Validators V(s) ⊆ Addr` declares the validator set as a sort of party identifiers; ISO 20022's PartyIdentification carries the party-identity aspect. Each member of V(s) corresponds to a PartyIdentification.

Direct (role aspect): being a validator is itself a role within the multiparty-validation policy; ISO 20022's PartyRole expresses the functional role a party plays. The same `Validators` symbol binds to two distinct ISO 20022 aspects — the party identity (PartyIdentification) and the validator role (PartyRole) — because membership in V(s) carries both.

relationships.note: Threshold validation rests on the broader access-control correctness framework — sound role-admin DAG, monotone delegation, effective revocation — that governs V and k.
Approval signatures must be existentially unforgeable; the cryptographic hardness is discharged here.
A multiparty-validated mint path satisfies both the supply-monotonicity invariant (BPO:0001) and the k-of-n approval invariant (this property) simultaneously.

attack_surface.pattern: the same signer's signature counted twice or more toward the threshold (e.g. via two distinct encodings, or two pubkey representations of the same identity)
attack_surface.notes: Distinct-signer counting must be over canonical signer identity, not over message-or-signature-bytes uniqueness.

attack_surface.pattern: approval signed when the signer was in V, executed after rotation removed them; or vice-versa
attack_surface.notes: Validate against V at execution time, or pin the relevant V via an approved-set commitment included in the signed message.

attack_surface.pattern: approval set valid for one transaction, contract, or chain replayed against another; missing nonce / chain-id / contract address in the signed payload
attack_surface.notes: EIP-712 domain separation including chain-id, verifyingContract, and a strictly-monotone nonce.

attack_surface.pattern: k or V reachable by a non-governance path (a forgotten setter, an unprotected initializer, a delegatecall write), defeating the guard out-of-band
attack_surface.notes: Enumerate every write path to k and V; require all to be authorized-governance per BPO:0040.

metrics: count(distinct authorized approvers) per privileged execution — must be ≥ k
invariant_checkpoints: post-effect: (V, k) unchanged unless the executed tx is a sanctioned governance update
runtime_assertions: assert(every counted signer ∈ V at execution block)

strategies.notes: Prove every privileged method's success path implies the threshold check holds against the current (V, k); prove (V, k) writes are themselves governance-gated.
Explore symbolic approval sets; confirm the threshold check is non-bypassable across all reachable selectors and bytecode paths.
Verify canonical-identity comparison in the signer-counting loop and reject patterns that count bytes-uniqueness in place of identity-uniqueness.

testability: k-1 valid signatures revert; k succeed
approval set containing a non-V signer reverts
approval replayed against a different tx-hash, chain-id, or contract reverts

runtime: EIP-712 domain-separated approval messages with nonces
validator-set membership check at execution block
static: linter rule: every privileged selector carries the threshold-check guard
design_patterns: batched approval verification before any state change
V commitment included in the signed message
two-step (V, k) update with a cooldown timelock

assumptions.statement: Approval signatures are existentially unforgeable at the deployed security parameter.
The validator set V and threshold k are themselves access-controlled; mutations occur only via the sanctioned governance path.
Approval messages carry sufficient domain separation (chain-id, contract address, nonce) so they are not replayable across chains, contracts, or operations.

provenance.notes: Authored to formalize the behavioural core of DASCP C16-S. The control's operational 'periodic updates' aspect is process and remains out of BPO scope.
